trial_title: Product Surveillance Registry- Deep Brain Stimulation for Epilepsy
brief_summary: The purpose of this observational registry is to evaluate the long-term effectiveness, safety and performance of market-released Medtronic Neuromodulation products for Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) for the treatment of refractory epilepsy. In addition, healthcare resource use and patient reported outcomes, such as health related quality of life will be assessed.

eligibility_table.criterion: Fulfilling the criteria of labeling indications of Medtronic® DBS™ Therapy for Epilepsy.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has a history of seizures but has not been diagnosed with refractory epilepsy as per the ILAE classification, as they have not had seizures for 20 years prior to the recent onset.

eligibility_table.criterion: Patient with diagnosis of refractory epilepsy as defined by 1981 ILAE (International League Against Epilepsy) classification, who have been implanted or will be implanted with Medtronic® DBS™ Therapy for Epilepsy.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient does not meet the criteria for refractory epilepsy since they have not had seizures for a significant period before the recent episodes.

eligibility_table.criterion: For both cohorts, completed at least two full consecutive months diary information on seizure type and frequency prior to DBS implant (seizure type should be classified at least as simple partial, complex partial, partial evolving to secondarily generalized seizures, and generalized). In regard to the prospective cohort, the patient will be conditionally enrolled at the enrolment visit, and the criterion will be reassessed at the baseline visit.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has not provided a seizure diary for at least two consecutive months prior to the DBS implant, which is required for eligibility.

eligibility_table.criterion: Patient or patient's legally authorized representative able to understand and to provide written informed consent and/or authorization for access to and use of health information, as required by an institution's IRB/MEC or local law and regulations.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient or their legally authorized representative can likely provide informed consent, assuming they understand the implications of the study.

eligibility_table.criterion: Incomplete and/or unreliable patient seizure diary based on the physician's judgment
eligibility_table.justification: The reliability of the patient's seizure diary is uncertain as full EEG reports are pending, and the physician's judgment on this is not available.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient documented seizure frequency in a diary with at least 80% reliability over the past three months according to the physician's assessment?

eligibility_table.criterion: Patient is currently enrolled in or plans to enroll in any concurrent drug, surgery and/or device study that may confound the results of this registry.
eligibility_table.justification: There is no information provided about concurrent enrollment in other studies, making it unclear whether this criterion is met.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is the patient currently enrolled in or planning to enroll in any concurrent drug, surgery, or device study that may confound the results of this registry?
